subject: Private offer renewal — commit shift, migration safety net & acceptance timing
messages:
From: Maria Alvarez <maria@ledgercorp.com>
To: nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@ledgercorp.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer renewal — acceptance window and commit shift

Hi Nikhil,

Hope you had a good weekend. We're working through the renewal for our private offer and need to align on two items before legal and procurement can push the PO through: 1) we need to move 25% of our committed capacity from the US pool to EU for data residency and latency once the new term starts; and 2) LedgerCorp wants an explicit migration safety net for the first 60 days to cover burst spikes during cutover.

Can Redwood confirm that:
- you can split the committed allocation across regions under one private-offer (no separate PO),
- the 60-day burst coverage can be scoped as a temporary credit applied to overage tokens while the migration settles, and
- acceptance window (we can accept the private offer) extends to May 10 so procurement has time for internal approvals.

Attached is our internal procurement checklist and a draft PO stub for reference (LedgerCorp_PO_2027Q2.pdf). If you can loop in legal/finance and advise on the process/timeline, that would help us finish our side.

Thanks,
Maria Alvarez
Head of Cloud Ops, LedgerCorp
(attachment: LedgerCorp_PO_2027Q2.pdf)

From: nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@ledgercorp.com>
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer renewal — acceptance window and commit shift

Maria — thanks for the clear note and the PO. Internal quick take below; looping Soojin (Marketplace) and Ben (Finance) to confirm specifics: 

Short answers up front:
- Yes, we can partition committed capacity by region under a single private offer and keep the same deal id; we treat region allocations as configurable on activation.
- We can provide a 60-day "migration safety net" implemented as credits that apply to overages (we'd convert to token credits that offset billable tokens).
- We can extend the acceptance window through May 10 on our side — confirm final signatory and we'll mark the HubSpot deal timeline.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben to confirm accounting treatment + any PO language needed for credit application (cc'd).
2) Soojin to prepare an activation playbook (staged cutover steps, KV cache priming notes) and a short SOW addendum describing the temporary burst coverage.
3) I'll send a consolidated term sheet (PrivateOffer_TermSheet_v3.docx) with proposed credit mechanics and the updated acceptance date.

Ben / Soojin — can you confirm by EOD today if finance/legal need different wording than "temporary credits applied to overage tokens for the first 60 days post-activation"?

Thanks — Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
(attachment: PrivateOffer_TermSheet_v3.docx)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Alvarez <maria@ledgercorp.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer renewal — acceptance window and commit shift

Nikhil / Soojin / Maria — quick finance check. We can agree to a 60-day credit as long as: 1) the applied credit is capped at a pre-agreed token amount (recommendation: cap = 40% of the Q2 committed quarterly tokens), and 2) credits are non-refundable and solely for offsetting overages.

Proposed PO language snippet: "Seller will allocate a migration credit pool equivalent to X tokens to be applied automatically against billed overage tokens for a period of 60 days following activation. Unused credits expire after the 60-day period."

Also: for our internal accounting we need the PO to reference the existing deal id (LDG-4782) and specify the regional split (%US/%EU). If LedgerCorp wants the 25% EU allocation to be adjustable post-activation, please mark that preference in the PO (we can support adjustments monthly).

If that sounds acceptable Maria, I can produce an invoice addendum and updated term sheet language for the DocuSign packet.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@ledgercorp.com>, nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer renewal — acceptance window and commit shift

Maria — thanks, we'll own the activation playbook. A few operational notes so LedgerCorp can plan cutover: 
- Staged activation recommended: route 10% of production traffic to EU nodes on day 1, 50% by day 7, full by day 30. This minimizes KV cache churn and lets us tune batch sizes.
- For the 60-day safety net, we'll implement automatic tagging so overage tokens during the window are flagged and credits applied before invoices are generated. We'll include runbook steps for rollback and emergency burst amplification.
- Need to confirm target instance types for EU pool (we recommend the c6g-optimized class for predictable latency).

I'll drop the activation playbook and a short checklist into the HubSpot deal and link in the term sheet. Maria — any constraints on staging cadence or maintenance blackout windows?

Best — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Marketplace Programs, Redwood Inference
(attachment: Activation_Playbook_v1.pdf — will upload to HubSpot)

From: Maria Alvarez <maria@ledgercorp.com>
To: nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@ledgercorp.com, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer renewal — acceptance window and commit shift

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement is OK with the credit cap approach, and our legal team approves the proposed PO language snippet. A couple of items from our side: 
- Please include a line in the PO noting that credits are "applied prior to invoicing and do not constitute a cash refund."
- We need the EU allocation to be adjustable in-month up to 10% without an amendment, as our traffic forecasts may change quickly during the migration. If Sierra from legal needs a clause, I can forward.

If Redwood can send the updated term sheet and a DocuSign packet with the PO stub + invoice addendum by Thursday EOD, procurement will route for signature and we should be able to accept by May 6 (giving a short buffer before your May 10 acceptance extension).

Appreciate the quick coordination — Maria
Maria Alvarez
Head of Cloud Ops, LedgerCorp
(attachment: LedgerCorp_Internal_Checklist.xlsx)
